events.note: Built 1967 as the first and only lookout structure on the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says staffed every summer. firelookout.com says presently available for emergencies. A May 27, 2022 visitor recorded no longer staffed. The date regular staffing ended is not given by any source, so this is not resolved; the story reports the disagreement.

cherylhill.net says the name comes from a discarded wagon tire beside the road; The Roaming Civic says an immigrant wagon was burned by indigenous people in the mid-1800s. Not used in the story; the accounts conflict.

sources.title: Wagontire Mountain – Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Built 1967 and BLM-administered are consistent across all four sources. Staffing is the open question: NHLR (undated) says staffed every summer; the May 2022 visitor says no longer staffed; firelookout.com says available for emergencies. No fire history or rental information found in the sources read. The cherylhill.net visitor thinks cameras were installed after the 2022 visit; not verified and left out. The Forest Lookouts page for Wagontire (oregonlookouts.weebly.com) was not read past the county index, so its 1967 entry is unverified. Brief had no height_m; none is in the sources read, so none is recorded.
